(A) Nuclear fusion: This is the process where two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus  and the energy is released because some of the matter is converted into energy.
(B) Nuclear fission: This is the process where a heavy nucleus splits into two or more smaller nuclei. It generally occurs for nuclei with higher atomic number (like Uranium or Plutonium). The energy is released because some of the matter is converted into energy.
(C) Beta decay : This is a type of radioactive decay that involves the conversion of a neutron into a proton or a proton into a neutron, accompanied by the emission of an electron or a positron, and a antineutrino or neutrino. This process is mediated by the weak nuclear force. The energy is released because some of the matter is converted into energy.
(D) Exothermic nuclear reaction: An exothermic nuclear reaction converts some matter into energy. Both fusion and fission are examples of highly exothermic Nuclear Reactions.
